The Role
Forward Deployed Engineers sit between our customers and our codebase. Some days you'll be in a working session with a compliance team learning how they actually run an alert to disposition; other days you'll be in our repos shipping the pipeline that makes that workflow ten times faster.
Roughly half of this job is building the core product alongside the rest of engineering. The other half is deploying, extending, and tuning it inside real customer environments. This is not a support or solutions role, you'll be held to the same engineering bar as everyone else on the team. The difference is that you will be the engineer that customers go to first, and the one who sees their problems firsthand.
What You'll Do
Build
Ship production code in the core platform alongside the rest of engineering including backend services, APIs, data pipelines, search
Design robust, well-architected APIs that power both our product and the integrations you deploy in the field
Build and productionize agent workflows and LLM-powered systems, including evals, guardrails, and cost/latency tuning
Operate what you build: instrumentation, observability, and SRE work when a pipeline breaks in a customer's environment at an inconvenient hour
Deploy
Embed with customers to learn their workflows, data, and constraints directly rather than through a requirements doc
Own technical delivery end to end: scoping, data onboarding, integration, deployment into their infrastructure, and the first weeks of production use
Bridge the current platform to customers with custom connectors, enrichment steps, migration scripts, internal tooling, etc
Be the credible technical voice in the room, whether you're talking to an analyst who has never seen an API or to their staff engineer who is skeptical of yours
Close the loop
Distinguish one-offs from the emerging pattern, and push patterns back into the core platform
Bring the field back to engineering, product, and leadership as evidence for what to prioritize
Set honest expectations with customers about what's shipping and when, and hold the line when the answer is "not soon"
Leave behind runbooks, docs, and internal write-ups so the next deployment is faster than the last

Proven ability to convert ad-hoc data requests into scalable, automated pipelines.
Experience working in the logistics domain.

The base pay range for this role is $140,000 to $160,000 annually. This range reflects the base pay that Loop reasonably expects to pay for the position at the time of hire. Proven expertise coding in
Embedded C/C++
and developing control algorithms using
MATLAB & Simulink
.

Hands-on experience with
CAN (J1939)
